learnings.title: GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles GA: pin direct and transitive action dependencies without changing readable refs
learnings.claim: GitHub announced on 2026-10-28 that GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfiles are generally available on Free, Team and Enterprise Cloud. The generated .github/workflows/actions.lock pins direct and transitive action dependencies to reviewed commits while workflows may retain readable tags; an onboarded workflow requires every action dependency in the lockfile. Lockfiles do not pin reusable workflow calls, runner images, inputs or secrets, and they do not establish that a dependency is safe. GitHub Docs says generate via gh actions-lock rather than editing manually.
learnings.decision: ACTIONS_LOCKFILE_ADOPTION_GATE: REVIEW_ONLY. Inventory workflow action refs and check for .github/workflows/actions.lock. If adoption is justified, use official gh actions-lock to generate a lockfile on a separate safe PR, review direct and transitive dependencies, preserve required checks, verify lockfile freshness in CI, and use full commit SHA for reusable workflow calls. Never hand-edit actions.lock or assume it secures runner images, inputs or secrets. Do not change workflow execution until tested.
learnings.next_measurement: System plan: audit .github/workflows for tag refs and reusable workflow calls, then test gh actions-lock against one non-critical workflow in a reviewed branch with exact CI run/HEAD SHA and applied_learning_ids in the actual system report. Current main has no .github/workflows/actions.lock; a read-only code search found actions/checkout@v4 in free-shorts-toolchain-smoke.yml. No workflow change in this promotion.
fallback_history: Until authorized lockfile adoption and CI proof, use reviewed full-length commit SHA pins for sensitive third-party actions and retain existing workflow protections.
